entries.title: Zero-based array indexing
entries.definition: Java array indices start at 0; an array of length N has valid indices 0 through N-1.
entries.mental_model: Length counts seats; indices are their zero-based labels.
entries.gotchas: Index N is outside an N-element array and throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
entries.notes: Lumen: the eighth bit occupies index 7, not index 8. This is why the bit loop uses b < 8.
entries.summary: Java array indices start at 0; an array of length N has valid indices 0 through N-1.

entries.title: Array length field
entries.definition: Read the number of elements in a Java array using its length field.
entries.mental_model: A two-dimensional array is an outer array of row arrays; outer length counts rows.
entries.gotchas:
Arrays use .length, not .length(). Strings use .length(). An empty 2D array has no row zero.

Using grid[0].length as the width of the entire grid assumes a nonempty rectangular grid with non-null rows. For jagged grids, use grid[row].length for each row.
entries.notes:
Lumen: flattenGlyph() uses grid.length for row count and grid[r].length for each row width.

For boolean[][] grid, grid.length counts rows and grid[0].length counts columns in row zero. Image coordinates reverse the naming order: x is column and y is row.
entries.summary: Read the number of elements in a Java array using its length field.

entries.title: Two-dimensional and jagged arrays
entries.definition: Represent a grid as an array containing arrays, which may have different lengths.
entries.mental_model: The outer array selects a row; the inner array selects a column.
entries.gotchas: A jagged array cannot safely be traversed using grid[0].length for every row. Rows can also be null if not initialized.
entries.notes: Lumen: boolean[][] stores true/false optical cells. flattenGlyph() supports rows with differing lengths.
entries.summary: Represent a grid as an array containing arrays, which may have different lengths.

entries.title: Index-controlled for loop
entries.definition: Iterate over valid array indices from zero up to, but excluding, length.
entries.mental_model: When starting at 0 and checking < length, the loop executes exactly length times.
entries.gotchas: Using i <= array.length performs one extra iteration and can access an invalid index.
entries.notes: Lumen: decodeBytes() must use b < 8 to read eight bits rather than nine.
entries.summary: Iterate over valid array indices from zero up to, but excluding, length.

entries.title: Enhanced for loop
entries.definition: Iterate directly over element values instead of manually computing an index.
entries.mental_model: Read each item in a collection in sequence.
entries.gotchas: An enhanced for loop does not directly provide the element index. Reassigning a primitive loop variable does not modify the original array.
entries.notes: Lumen: for (boolean[] row : grid) neatly sums each row.length before allocating a flat array.
entries.summary: Iterate directly over element values instead of manually computing an index.

entries.title: Nested for loops for grids
entries.signature: for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) { for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) { ... } }
entries.definition: Use an outer loop for rows and an inner loop for elements within each row.
entries.mental_model: Each outer-loop step starts a complete inner-loop traversal.
entries.gotchas: Keep r/c coordinate meanings consistent; image X usually corresponds to column, image Y to row.
entries.notes:
Lumen: used in both GlyphRenderer and GlyphDecoder to traverse the same cell positions.

To populate a fresh rectangular boolean grid, allocate new boolean[rows][columns], then assign each grid[row][column] inside the inner loop. Each row runs its own full column loop. For image sampling, keep row mapped to y and column mapped to x; the assigned expression must produce boolean.
entries.summary: Use an outer loop for rows and an inner loop for elements within each row.

entries.title: Row-major mapping and write cursor
entries.signature: flatIndex = row * columns + column; / flat[index++] = grid[row][column];
entries.definition: Map a rectangular grid to a flat array, or maintain an incrementing write cursor for variable-length rows.
entries.mental_model: Read shelves in order and put every item in the next empty slot.
entries.gotchas: row * columns + column only works for uniform row widths; a cursor works with jagged arrays if output size was allocated correctly.
entries.notes: Lumen: toGrid() uses division/modulus for flat-to-grid mapping; flattenGlyph() uses an index cursor for grid-to-flat copying.
entries.summary: Map a rectangular grid to a flat array, or maintain an incrementing write cursor for variable-length rows.

entries.title: Ceiling division for positive counts
entries.definition: Calculate the number of groups needed when a partial final group still requires space.
entries.mental_model: Divide, but round upward so leftovers get their own container.
entries.gotchas: This formula assumes count >= 0 and perGroup > 0; count + perGroup - 1 can overflow int for huge values.
entries.notes: Lumen: toGrid() determines the required row count from bit count and chosen column count.
entries.summary: Calculate the number of groups needed when a partial final group still requires space.

entries.title: Remainder operator (%)
entries.definition: Return the remainder of integer division.
entries.mental_model: The quotient tells you which group; the remainder tells you the position within that group.
entries.return_value: int or long for integer operands
entries.gotchas: Using zero as the divisor throws ArithmeticException. Java remainder can be negative for negative dividends.
entries.notes: Lumen: column = bitIndex % columns maps a flat bit position into a glyph column.
entries.summary: Return the remainder of integer division.

entries.title: Default boolean array values
entries.definition: Newly allocated boolean arrays contain false in every element until assigned.
entries.mental_model: An unused boolean slot starts cleared.
entries.gotchas: Defaults are properties of array elements and object fields; uninitialized local boolean variables cannot be read.
entries.notes: Lumen: any unused padding cells in a newly allocated boolean grid start as false; decoding must still know the actual data length.
entries.summary: Newly allocated boolean arrays contain false in every element until assigned.

entries.title: Unsigned right shift (>>>)
entries.definition: Shift an integer right, filling vacated high bits with zeros.
entries.mental_model: Move the visible bit pattern right without copying the sign bit.
entries.return_value: int or long after numeric promotion
entries.gotchas: Java promotes byte and short operands to int before shifting. >>> differs from >> for negative values.
entries.notes: Lumen: encodeByte() extracts bits most-significant first using (value >>> i) & 1.
entries.summary: Shift an integer right, filling vacated high bits with zeros.

entries.title: Left shift (<<)
entries.definition: Shift integer bits left, filling newly exposed low bits with zeros.
entries.mental_model: Each left shift makes space for incoming bits.
entries.return_value: int or long after numeric promotion
entries.gotchas: High bits may be discarded; overflow can change the sign. byte and short are promoted to int. Shift distances are masked by type width.
entries.notes: Lumen: decodeBytes() shifts the accumulating number left before appending another bit.
entries.summary: Shift integer bits left, filling newly exposed low bits with zeros.

entries.title: Bitwise AND (&)
entries.definition: Apply AND to each corresponding pair of integer bits; a result bit is 1 only if both inputs have 1.
entries.mental_model: A bitmask acts as a stencil that keeps only selected bits.
entries.return_value: integer result (or boolean for boolean operands)
entries.gotchas: & also operates on booleans (without short-circuiting). Use && for ordinary short-circuit logical conditions.
entries.notes: Lumen: (value >>> i) & 1 isolates a single extracted bit.
entries.summary: Apply AND to each corresponding pair of integer bits; a result bit is 1 only if both inputs have 1.

entries.title: Bitwise OR (|)
entries.definition: Apply OR to integer bits; each output bit is 1 if either input bit is 1.
entries.mental_model: Turn on selected bit positions without clearing the other positions.
entries.return_value: integer result (or boolean for boolean operands)
entries.gotchas: | also supports booleans, but does not short-circuit. Do not confuse it with ||.
entries.notes: Lumen: decodeBytes() appends the next numeric bit after shifting the accumulator.
entries.summary: Apply OR to integer bits; each output bit is 1 if either input bit is 1.

entries.title: Accumulate bits into an integer
entries.definition: Build a binary integer from most-significant-bit-first input by shifting and appending each bit.
entries.mental_model: The accumulator remembers all previous bits; a new bit is placed at the rightmost end.
entries.gotchas: Initialize once per completed value, not once per input bit. Ensure input bitValue is 0 or 1.
entries.notes: Lumen: decodeBytes() accumulates exactly eight bits before storing a byte and resetting the accumulator.
entries.summary: Build a binary integer from most-significant-bit-first input by shifting and appending each bit.

entries.title: Ternary conditional operator (?:)
entries.definition: Select one of two expressions based on a boolean condition.
entries.mental_model: A compact expression-level if/else that produces a value.
entries.gotchas: A ternary expression can become hard to read when nested. Branch types influence the resulting expression type.
entries.notes: Lumen: booleanBit ? 1 : 0 converts a boolean cell into a numeric bit.
entries.summary: Select one of two expressions based on a boolean condition.

entries.title: Explicit primitive cast to byte
entries.definition: Narrow an integer value to Java byte, keeping only the low eight bits.
entries.mental_model: Casting to byte stores the low eight bits in a signed eight-bit container.
entries.gotchas: Java byte is signed (-128 to 127). Narrowing does not check for lost high bits.
entries.notes:
Lumen: decodeBytes() stores the completed int accumulator with byteArray[u] = (byte) number.

Related narrowing conversion: int position = (int) distance; explicitly converts a double to int. For finite values within the int range, this discards the fractional part toward zero: 9.8 becomes 9 and -9.8 becomes -9. It does not round to the nearest integer. When calculating a fractional cell width, use (double) width / columns before the final coordinate cast. Assigning width / columns to double, or casting that integer quotient afterward, cannot restore a lost fraction. Keep cell dimensions as double until the point where an integer pixel coordinate is required.
entries.summary: Narrow an integer value to Java byte, keeping only the low eight bits.

entries.title: Post-increment operator (++)
entries.definition: Increment a numeric variable by one, returning its previous value in expression context.
entries.mental_model: Advance the write cursor after using its current slot.
entries.gotchas: index++ and ++index both increment but yield different expression values. Use a separate line when clarity matters.
entries.notes: Lumen: flattenGlyph() uses index++ after copying each cell into a flat bit array.
entries.summary: Increment a numeric variable by one, returning its previous value in expression context.

entries.title: Arrays.equals()
entries.definition: Compare the lengths and corresponding elements of one-dimensional arrays.
entries.mental_model: Compare the contents of two containers, not whether they are the same object.
entries.gotchas: Array == checks reference identity, not element contents. For arrays of arrays, use Arrays.deepEquals().
entries.notes: Lumen: compares original and optically recovered bits/bytes to verify an exact round trip.
entries.summary: Compare the lengths and corresponding elements of one-dimensional arrays.

entries.title: Arrays.deepEquals()
entries.definition: Compare nested arrays recursively, including multi-dimensional primitive arrays.
entries.mental_model: Inspect the items inside each row rather than comparing row-object identities.
entries.gotchas: Arrays.equals(a, b) on boolean[][] only compares row references; deepEquals is needed to compare cell contents.
entries.notes: Lumen: verifies decodedGrid has the same boolean cells as the source grid.
entries.summary: Compare nested arrays recursively, including multi-dimensional primitive arrays.

entries.title: Arrays.toString()
entries.definition: Produce a readable string of the elements in a one-dimensional array for debugging.
entries.mental_model: Turn a row of values into a printable diagnostic label.
entries.gotchas: For nested arrays use Arrays.deepToString(). The output is for human readability, not a stable binary format.
entries.notes: Lumen: printed original/recovered boolean arrays and byte arrays while debugging the first optical glyph.
entries.summary: Produce a readable string of the elements in a one-dimensional array for debugging.

entries.title: BufferedImage
entries.definition:
Store an image with writable/readable pixel data in Java memory.

getWidth() and getHeight() return int pixel counts. Width corresponds to x/columns; height corresponds to y/rows.
entries.mental_model: A two-dimensional pixel canvas whose width is measured horizontally and height vertically.
entries.gotchas: Width and height must be positive. Image coordinates start at (0,0) in the top-left; X increases right, Y increases down.
entries.notes:
Lumen: GlyphRenderer draws a boolean[][] grid onto a BufferedImage.

Valid pixel coordinates run from x = 0 to width - 1 and y = 0 to height - 1. Use these dimensions when choosing coordinates for getRGB(x, y).
entries.summary: Store an image with writable/readable pixel data in Java memory.

entries.title: BufferedImage.getRGB()
entries.definition: Read a pixel as a packed 32-bit ARGB integer.
entries.mental_model: Choose a pixel by horizontal X and vertical Y, then read its packed color.
entries.gotchas: getRGB can throw if coordinates are out of range. Exact black comparisons are suitable for lossless synthetic images, but real camera images need thresholds.
entries.notes: Lumen: readGrid() samples each cell center using centerX = col * cellSize + cellSize/2 and centerY = row * cellSize + cellSize/2.
entries.summary: Read a pixel as a packed 32-bit ARGB integer.

entries.title: Graphics2D.fillRect()
entries.definition: Draw a filled rectangle using the current Graphics2D paint/color.
entries.mental_model: Place a solid colored tile at a chosen pixel rectangle.
entries.gotchas: Graphics2D uses x/y coordinates, not row/column. Dispose of graphics contexts after drawing.
entries.notes: Lumen: fillRect(col * cellSize, row * cellSize, cellSize, cellSize) renders individual optical cells.
entries.summary: Draw a filled rectangle using the current Graphics2D paint/color.

entries.title: Color.getRGB()
entries.definition: Obtain a packed ARGB integer representing an AWT Color.
entries.mental_model: A named paint color can also be represented as a single integer.
entries.gotchas: Packed ARGB integers are signed Java ints; negative values are normal and do not mean an invalid color.
entries.notes: Lumen: GlyphDecoder compares the synthetic image pixel integer with Color.BLACK.getRGB().
entries.summary: Obtain a packed ARGB integer representing an AWT Color.

entries.title: ImageIO.write()
entries.definition: Encode a RenderedImage into a file using an available image writer.
entries.mental_model: Convert an in-memory pixel canvas into a persistent image file.
entries.gotchas: ImageIO.write() can return false if no encoder exists for the format and can throw IOException on write errors.
entries.notes: Lumen: saves the first load-bearing optical glyph to PNG for round-trip validation.
entries.summary: Encode a RenderedImage into a file using an available image writer.

entries.title: ImageIO.read()
entries.definition: Decode a supported image file into a BufferedImage.
entries.mental_model: Turn an image file back into an in-memory pixel canvas.
entries.gotchas: May return null if no reader recognizes the input. Can throw IOException when file access or decoding fails.
entries.notes: Lumen: reads loadBearingGlyph.png back into memory before sampling and decoding its cells.
entries.summary: Decode a supported image file into a BufferedImage.

entries.title: readAllBytes()
entries.definition: Return a byte[] containing the file's bytes in order, without decoding text or changing line endings.
entries.mental_model: Keep the original byte content intact until you choose how to interpret it.
entries.gotchas: Reads the whole file into memory and can throw IOException. Java byte values are signed, but their eight-bit patterns are preserved.
entries.notes: Lumen: read the source bytes before encoding them. This does not change the source file.
entries.summary: Read an entire file as raw bytes.

entries.title: write()
entries.definition: Write the byte[] content in order. With no options, create a missing file or truncate an existing file before writing.
entries.mental_model: Replace the destination's content with these bytes.
entries.gotchas: The default does not append. Existing content is replaced, even when the new array is shorter. Can throw IOException; a failed write may leave partial output.
entries.notes: Lumen: write recovered bytes to a separate output path.
entries.summary: Write a byte array to a file.

entries.title: Color(int RGB)
entries.definition: Color(int RGB) reads the packed red, green, and blue components. getRed(), getGreen(), and getBlue() each return an int from 0 through 255.
entries.mental_model: Unpack one pixel value into three separately named channel values.
entries.return_value: Color from construction; int from each channel getter
entries.gotchas: The one-int constructor makes the Color opaque; it does not preserve the input's alpha channel.
entries.notes: Lumen: pass image.getRGB(x, y) to this constructor before computing the prototype RGB average.
entries.summary: Construct a Color from a packed RGB integer and read its channels.

entries.title: RGB arithmetic mean and dark threshold
entries.signature: double average = (red + green + blue) / 3.0; boolean dark = average < threshold;
entries.definition: Add the three RGB channel values and divide by 3.0 to obtain a double arithmetic mean. The < comparison returns true when that mean is below the threshold.
entries.mental_model: Reduce three channel numbers to one rough brightness number, then ask whether it is low enough to count as dark.
entries.gotchas: Dividing int operands by 3 performs integer division first, even if assigned to a double. Equality with the threshold produces false for <. An unweighted RGB mean is a prototype heuristic, not calibrated luminance.
entries.notes:
Lumen convention: true means a dark cell. The example threshold is illustrative, not a camera calibration.

A relational comparison already produces a boolean. In a boolean-returning method, return mean < threshold; is equivalent to if (mean < threshold) return true; else return false;. With strict <, a mean equal to the threshold returns false.
entries.summary: Use double division and a comparison to classify a sampled pixel.

entries.title: String(byte[], Charset)
entries.definition: Create a String by interpreting the byte[] with UTF-8. StandardCharsets.UTF_8 makes the intended encoding explicit.
entries.mental_model: The bytes are the stored content; the character set tells Java how to read them as text.
entries.gotchas: Use the encoding that matches the data. This constructor replaces malformed sequences, so printed text alone cannot prove byte equality. Use Arrays.equals for an exact byte comparison.
entries.notes: Lumen: decode recovered text for inspection while keeping the original byte[] for verification.
entries.summary: Decode bytes as text using an explicit character set.

entries.title: Logical OR (||) and throwing guards
entries.definition: || is true when either operand is true. It short-circuits: the right operand is evaluated only if the left is false. A throwing guard prevents invalid input from reaching the following statements.
entries.mental_model: Either invalid condition closes the gate; reaching the next line means both checks passed.
entries.return_value: boolean from ||; throw exits the normal flow
entries.gotchas: After this guard, sequenceNumber == 0 and totalPackets == 1 follow only while those values remain unchanged. An IDE may mark a repeated check as always true because of the earlier throw; that is control-flow reasoning, not a declaration of a constant.
entries.notes:
Lumen: this guard describes the current single-packet prototype, not a general multi-packet protocol.

Grid-reading guards: reject rows <= 0 || columns <= 0 before allocating or dividing by these counts. For a reader that requires at least one image pixel per cell in each direction, also reject width < columns || height < rows. After these guards, width / (double) columns and height / (double) rows are each at least 1.0. Equal image and grid dimensions are allowed. Zero-length arrays are legal Java, but this reader requires positive dimensions; this is an input rule, not a general ban on empty arrays.
entries.summary: Reject invalid input when either of two checks fails.

entries.title: main() entry point and IOException
entries.signature: public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException
entries.definition: The traditional public static void main(String[] args) declaration works across Java versions. A throws IOException clause allows checked I/O failures to propagate out of main.
entries.mental_model: main is where the launcher begins executing your program; throws describes a possible exceptional exit.
entries.gotchas: Declaring throws does not recover from an error. Java 25 also accepts package-access static void main(String[] args) and static void main(); omitting public is valid there but is not portable to older launchers.
entries.notes: Lumen's existing Java 25 package-access static main is valid. The public form is useful for portable examples. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se25/html/jls-12.html#jls-12.1.4
entries.summary: Recognize the portable main declaration and Java 25's package-access form.

entries.title: IO.println() (Java 25)
entries.definition: Java 25's java.lang.IO provides static println(Object) and println() methods for standard output. IO is automatically available through java.lang in ordinary source files.
entries.mental_model: A short standard-output helper for line-based output.
entries.gotchas: Requires Java 25 or later. System.out.println remains the familiar option across older Java versions.
entries.notes: Verified against the Java 25 API and the installed OpenJDK 25 runtime. Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/IO.html
entries.summary: Print a value and a line separator with java.lang.IO.

entries.title: @main entry point and Unit
entries.definition: @main generates a launchable entry point for the annotated method. A Unit result indicates that the method does not return a useful value.
entries.mental_model: The launcher starts here; println performs the visible work.
entries.gotchas: This is Scala 3 syntax. Unit is a type; () is the Unit value.
entries.summary: Mark a Scala 3 method as a program entry point.

entries.title: String literals and interpolation
entries.definition: An s-prefixed string substitutes $name or ${expression}. Ordinary quoted strings recognize escapes such as \n. Triple-quoted strings can span lines and keep embedded quotes without backslash escaping.
entries.mental_model: Choose the literal form for the text, then explicitly request interpolation with s when needed.
entries.gotchas: Triple quotes alone do not interpolate variables. Their literal newlines and indentation become part of the string.
entries.summary: Embed values in text and write quoted or multiline text.

entries.title: Singleton objects and private members
entries.signature: object Name: ...; private val ...; private def ...
entries.definition: object defines a singleton instance. Call its members with Name.member without creating an instance with new. A colon can open an indentation-based object body in Scala 3; braces are also supported. private keeps a member internal to its defining scope.
entries.mental_model: One named object exposes selected operations and keeps its implementation helpers inside.
entries.gotchas: Indentation determines the body when using the colon form. Callers cannot directly use a private helper.
entries.summary: Group members in a singleton and restrict internal helpers.

entries.title: Type arguments in square brackets
entries.definition: Square brackets supply type arguments. List[String] contains Strings, while Map[String, Int] maps String keys to Int values. The same syntax describes Java generic results such as HttpResponse[String].
entries.mental_model: The outer type names the container; the bracketed types describe what it holds.
entries.gotchas: Square brackets specify types; parentheses supply value arguments to a call.
entries.summary: Supply element, key/value, and result types to generic types.

entries.title: if / then / else expressions
entries.signature: if condition then valueA else valueB
entries.definition: An if expression evaluates a Boolean condition and produces the value of the chosen branch. Use else if for another condition.
entries.mental_model: Each branch supplies the result assigned to the surrounding expression.
entries.gotchas: For a String result, make every possible branch produce the intended String rather than ending with a Unit-valued statement.
entries.summary: Choose a value with Scala 3 conditional syntax.

entries.title: Closures and no-argument function types
entries.definition: () => Int is the type of a function taking no arguments and returning Int. A lambda can capture a surrounding variable and retain access after the enclosing method returns.
entries.mental_model: The returned function carries access to the local counter it uses.
entries.gotchas: A captured var is shared across calls to that particular closure. Separate createCounter calls create separate local counters.
entries.summary: Return a function that retains access to local state.

entries.title: Tuples and destructuring lambdas
entries.definition: A tuple groups values with a type for each position. _1 and _2 read the first and second components. A case (key, value) lambda in map matches and names those components.
entries.mental_model: A small positional bundle can be projected or unpacked into local names.
entries.gotchas: The case syntax here is a pattern-matching lambda accepted by map; it need not have the PartialFunction type.
entries.summary: Group values and unpack a tuple in a mapping function.

entries.title: try / catch / finally
entries.signature: try ... catch case e: ExceptionType => ... finally ...
entries.definition: catch uses case clauses to match thrown exceptions. case e: ExceptionType binds the exception; case _: ExceptionType matches without retaining it. finally runs cleanup when control leaves the try/catch.
entries.mental_model: Try the operation, handle a matching failure, and release resources in finally.
entries.gotchas: Use the relevant exception type and keep cleanup separate from the useful result expression.
entries.summary: Handle exceptions with type patterns and run cleanup.

entries.title: Grouped imports
entries.definition: Braces inside an import select multiple members from the same package. This is Scala import syntax even when the imported types are Java APIs.
entries.mental_model: Write the shared package once and list the required names.
entries.summary: Import several names from one package together.

entries.title: mkString()
entries.definition: mkString inserts the chosen separator between element representations. A newline, comma-space, or ampersand can join different kinds of output.
entries.mental_model: Many values become one piece of text.
entries.gotchas: Joining query or form pieces does not encode them; encode each component before joining when required.
entries.summary: Join collection elements into one String.

entries.title: Array allocation and mutable contents
entries.definition: Array[Byte] is an array type; new Array[Byte](32) allocates 32 byte slots. val prevents rebinding the array variable, but APIs can still modify the existing array contents.
entries.mental_model: The reference stays fixed while the array it points to can be filled.
entries.gotchas: SecureRandom.nextBytes mutates its supplied array; it does not return the populated byte array. SecureRandom is a Java API, while the Array type and allocation syntax are Scala.
entries.summary: Allocate a typed array whose contents can change through a val reference.

entries.title: Flattening optional collection results
entries.definition: A List.flatMap function returning Option contributes one element for Some and zero for None. toList converts an array to a List; flatten removes one nested collection or Option layer.
entries.mental_model: Collect the present results into one list instead of a list of wrappers.
entries.gotchas: Do not silently discard malformed security parameters with None/flatMap when they should cause rejection.
entries.summary: Combine optional parser results into a flat collection.

entries.title: exists(), distinct(), and size
entries.definition: exists asks whether any element satisfies a predicate. distinct removes duplicate values; size counts elements. Comparing sizes before and after distinct detects duplicates.
entries.mental_model: Ask whether any item is invalid and whether removing repetitions changes the count.
entries.gotchas: Check duplicate keys before converting key/value pairs to a Map, which would collapse duplicates.
entries.summary: Check for invalid elements and duplicate values.

entries.title: String splitting and length checks
entries.definition: On the JVM, String.split uses the Java String API. A positive limit of 2 keeps later delimiters in the second part; a negative limit preserves trailing empty parts. String.length counts UTF-16 code units on the JVM; isEmpty/nonEmpty test emptiness.
entries.mental_model: Choose how much structure to split before validating each part.
entries.return_value: Array[String] from split; Int length; Boolean emptiness
entries.gotchas: The split delimiter is a regular expression. For raw query text, split into components first, then decode individual parts.
entries.summary: Control split limits and inspect string lengths or emptiness.

entries.title: UTF-8 file export
entries.definition: Path.of describes the output location; Files.writeString encodes the text with the supplied charset and writes it to that file.
entries.mental_model: Scala calls the Java API with ordinary method calls and explicit types.
entries.gotchas: With no open options, an existing file is truncated/replaced. Use an intentional output path.
entries.notes: Java/JDK API used from Scala; not an intrinsic Scala language feature.
entries.summary: Write a String using Java NIO and an explicit charset.

entries.title: HttpClient requests and responses
entries.definition: HttpClient.send is synchronous. BodyHandlers.ofString produces HttpResponse[String]; body() returns String and statusCode() returns Int. Builders configure the URI, HTTP method, headers, and optional body publisher before build().
entries.mental_model: Scala calls the Java API with ordinary method calls and explicit types.
entries.return_value: HttpRequest from build; HttpResponse[String] from send
entries.gotchas: An HTTP error status can arrive as an ordinary response, not an exception. Inspect statusCode(). Use application/x-www-form-urlencoded for form bodies. Bearer is followed by a space and the token; never log or hard-code real tokens in examples.
entries.notes: Java/JDK API used from Scala; not an intrinsic Scala language feature.
entries.summary: Build GET/POST requests, set headers, and inspect typed responses.

entries.title: URL form component encoding and decoding
entries.definition: URLEncoder and URLDecoder apply form-style component encoding. Use the same charset for both directions.
entries.mental_model: Scala calls the Java API with ordinary method calls and explicit types.
entries.gotchas: Split a raw query first, then decode its individual keys and values; decoding before splitting can turn encoded data into separators. These APIs do not encode a whole URL as one component.
entries.notes: Java/JDK API used from Scala; not an intrinsic Scala language feature.
entries.summary: Encode/decode individual form or query components with UTF-8.

entries.title: Random bytes, SHA-256, and Base64url
entries.definition: SecureRandom fills an existing byte array. MessageDigest with SHA-256 hashes input bytes deterministically. The URL-safe Base64 encoder converts bytes to text; withoutPadding omits padding characters.
entries.mental_model: Scala calls the Java API with ordinary method calls and explicit types.
entries.return_value: Array[Byte] from digest; String from encodeToString
entries.gotchas: Generating random verifier material and hashing a verifier are different steps. An array toString is not a byte encoding. The example is a generic API demonstration, not a complete authentication flow.
entries.notes: Java/JDK API used from Scala; not an intrinsic Scala language feature.
entries.summary: Distinguish random byte generation, hashing, and text encoding.

entries.title: HttpServer lifecycle and handler lambdas
entries.definition: HttpHandler is a Java single-abstract-method interface, so a compatible typed Scala lambda can implement it. Register contexts before starting the server. HttpExchange exposes the request method and URI, and response headers/body operations.
entries.mental_model: Scala calls the Java API with ordinary method calls and explicit types.
entries.return_value: HttpServer from create; Unit for lifecycle and response actions
entries.gotchas: Reading or printing a request is not a complete HTTP response. Set headers before sendResponseHeaders, use the UTF-8 byte count (converted to Long with .toLong), and close the response stream in finally. getRawQuery can return Java null.
entries.notes: Java/JDK API used from Scala; not an intrinsic Scala language feature.
entries.summary: Adapt a Scala lambda to HttpHandler and manage a local Java HTTP server.

entries.title: CompletableFuture completion and waiting
entries.definition: complete returns true only when it performs the completion; later attempts return false. completeExceptionally records a failure. get waits and returns the result, or throws for failure, timeout, or interruption.
entries.mental_model: Scala calls the Java API with ordinary method calls and explicit types.
entries.return_value: Boolean from completion; the result type from get
entries.gotchas: ExecutionException wraps the underlying failure. TimeoutException and InterruptedException are separate outcomes; restore the thread interrupt flag when handling an interruption without propagating it. This Java class differs from scala.concurrent.Future.
entries.notes: Java/JDK API used from Scala; not an intrinsic Scala language feature.
entries.summary: Complete a Java future once and wait with a timeout.

entries.title: ujson.read and typed value access
entries.definition: ujson.read parses text into ujson.Value. Property access selects a value; .str expects a JSON string, and .num expects a number and returns Double. Scala .toInt converts that Double to Int.
entries.mental_model: Parse the document, select the field, then request the expected value type.
entries.gotchas: Missing fields or the wrong JSON type can fail access. .toInt is conversion, not validation that the source number was integral; for ordinary finite in-range values it truncates a fraction toward zero.
entries.notes: External library API. Examples use the conversation's uJson 4.4.3 dependency.
entries.summary: Parse JSON and extract expected string and numeric fields.

entries.title: Nested JSON arrays to Scala collections
entries.definition: Successive property accesses traverse nested JSON objects. .arr is a uJson accessor; .toList and .map are Scala collection operations used after selecting the JSON array.
entries.mental_model: Follow the JSON shape first, then transform each element into the desired Scala value.
entries.gotchas: Each object, array, and string accessor assumes the expected JSON shape. This small example does not implement an exporter or pagination.
entries.summary: Traverse expected JSON objects and map their arrays to typed Lists.

entries.title: Absent JSON fields versus JSON null
entries.definition: .obj.get returns None when an object key is absent. If the key exists with explicit JSON null, it returns Some(ujson.Null); that value is not a string, so .str fails. A present value of another wrong type also fails .str. For a present field, case ujson.Str(url) extracts string content and case ujson.Null handles JSON null explicitly.
entries.mental_model: Missing key and present-but-null are different JSON states.
entries.return_value: Option[String] only when present values have the expected string type
entries.gotchas: Some(incoming("next").str) is unsafe for JSON null: .str is evaluated before Some is constructed. Neither Some(...) nor Option(...) catches an exception from its argument. The absent-field example handles missing keys only; it is not a completed pagination parser. Direct incoming("next") still assumes the key exists. Handle unexpected JSON types explicitly rather than assuming the Str/Null cases cover every input.
entries.summary: Use object lookup for an absent field and recognize its limits.

entries.title: Scala CLI dependency directives
entries.definition: Scala CLI recognizes specially formatted comment directives to configure a build. using dep adds a dependency; the double colon requests the artifact matching the Scala binary version.
entries.mental_model: A tool-readable comment supplies build configuration alongside the source.
entries.gotchas: This is Scala CLI tooling syntax, not a Scala language keyword or an sbt setting. Version 4.4.3 is the version used in the conversation, not a claim about the latest available release.
entries.summary: Declare an external dependency for Scala CLI.

entries.title: RFLAGS and condition results
entries.definition: Arithmetic flags describe a result, not a permanent property of a register. CF tracks unsigned carry/borrow; OF tracks signed range overflow; ZF marks zero; SF copies the high result bit; PF reports even parity of the low byte; AF tracks the low-nibble carry. Only rely on flags explicitly defined by the instruction. Save a condition with SETcc before later arithmetic overwrites it.
entries.mental_model: Separate the result bits from the interpretation: 0x80000000 can be a large unsigned value or a negative signed value.
entries.return_value: ADD defines six arithmetic flags. SETO/MOVZX preserve them.
entries.gotchas: PUSHFQ/POPFQ are not general privilege-changing tools. Do not use undefined flags from MUL/IMUL/IDIV as conditions.
entries.notes:
Scope: x86-64.
Debugger exercise: stop after ADD and inspect eflags. Compare unsigned carry to signed overflow. The trace only reads ordinary user-mode flags.
Related: ADD and SUB; CMP; SETcc.
Official references: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html
https://www.nasm.us/doc/nasm03.html
Local lab: assemble this demo to ELF64 and link to a matching C harness. Break at demo; use stepi, info registers and objdump -dr to compare the annotated state. No instruction fragment is a standalone executable without its harness.
entries.summary: Arithmetic flags describe a result, not a permanent property of a register.

entries.title: INC and DEC preserve carry
entries.definition: INC/DEC add/subtract one at the destination width. They update OF,SF,ZF,AF,PF while leaving CF exactly as it was. This differs from ADD/SUB by one and matters in multiword arithmetic. A count decrement that reaches zero can drive JNZ; test an externally supplied zero count before entering a loop.
entries.mental_model: A one-step counter update has a deliberately different flag contract from general addition.
entries.return_value: DEC defines OF,SF,ZF,AF,PF, preserves CF. STC sets CF only.
entries.gotchas: Using DEC where the next instruction expects fresh borrow information from SUB is wrong. Zero-count decrement loops can wrap.
entries.notes:
Scope: x86-64.

Related: Labels; ADC and SBB.
Official references: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html
https://www.nasm.us/doc/nasm03.html
Local lab: assemble this demo to ELF64 and link to a matching C harness. Break at demo; use stepi, info registers and objdump -dr to compare the annotated state. No instruction fragment is a standalone executable without its harness.
entries.summary: INC/DEC add/subtract one at the destination width.

entries.title: ADC and SBB across words
entries.definition: ADC adds source plus incoming CF; SBB subtracts source plus incoming CF. Chain low word first, then high word, so carry/borrow propagates. Keep instructions that overwrite CF out of the chain. This permits a 128-bit sum using two 64-bit halves without requiring a 128-bit integer register.
entries.mental_model: The carry flag is the single bit crossing the boundary between adjacent words.
entries.return_value: ADD/ADC/SUB/SBB define CF,OF,SF,ZF,AF,PF. Final flags describe the high-word operation, not the whole 128-bit value.
entries.gotchas: Testing only final ZF does not tell whether the whole multiword result is zero. OR copies of both halves for that test.
entries.notes:
Scope: x86-64.

Related: ADD and SUB; RFLAGS and condition results.
Official references: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html
https://www.nasm.us/doc/nasm03.html
Local lab: assemble this demo to ELF64 and link to a matching C harness. Break at demo; use stepi, info registers and objdump -dr to compare the annotated state. No instruction fragment is a standalone executable without its harness.
entries.summary: ADC adds source plus incoming CF; SBB subtracts source plus incoming CF.

entries.title: NEG and two’s-complement limits
entries.definition: NEG computes 0 minus its operand at the same width. Most signed values have a representable negation; the minimum signed value does not. NEG sets CF unless its input was zero, and sets OF for the minimum signed input. NOT alone is bitwise inversion, not arithmetic negation; two’s-complement negation corresponds to inversion plus one.
entries.mental_model: The bit pattern wraps, so detecting overflow is a separate step.
entries.return_value: NEG defines CF,OF,SF,ZF,AF,PF as subtraction from zero.
entries.gotchas: A hand-written absolute value must decide what to do with the minimum signed integer. Widening first can change what fits.
entries.notes:
Scope: x86-64.

Related: Signed division; General-purpose registers.
Official references: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html
https://www.nasm.us/doc/nasm03.html

entries.summary: NEG computes 0 minus its operand at the same width.

entries.title: Shifts, rotates, and count-dependent flags
entries.definition: SHL shifts toward the high end; SHR inserts zeros at the high end; SAR repeats the sign bit. Nonzero one-bit shifts put the shifted-out bit in CF and define SF/ZF/PF from the result, with AF undefined. For count 1: SHL OF=MSB(result) XOR CF; SHR OF=old MSB; SAR OF=0. For larger counts OF is undefined. ROL/ROR rotate bits instead of discarding them; they affect CF and, for count 1, OF, but preserve SF/ZF/AF/PF.
entries.mental_model: A shift is a bit operation with width/count rules; signed rounding may differ from division.
entries.return_value: The SAR count here is 1. An effective count of 0 changes neither operand nor flags. Avoid relying on CF for shifts at/above operand width.
entries.gotchas: Counts are masked, not bounded by a high-level range check. An immediate shift by 32 on a 32-bit operand has effective count zero.
entries.notes:
Scope: x86-64.
Debugger exercise: compare SAR and SHR of 0xfffffffd, then compare with signed IDIV. Do not infer multi-bit OF from a debugger display.
Related: Bitwise operations; idiv.
Official references: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html
https://www.nasm.us/doc/nasm03.html

entries.title: SETcc produces a byte boolean
entries.definition: SETcc writes 0 or 1 to a byte register/memory operand using a flag condition. It does not clear the rest of a larger register. Use MOVZX to turn its byte result into a full-width numeric boolean. SETL/SETB distinguish signed and unsigned comparison exactly like JL/JB.
entries.mental_model: Materialize a condition before later arithmetic changes the flags.
entries.return_value: SETcc and MOVZX preserve the flags set by CMP.
entries.gotchas: Returning AL alone leaves higher bits unrelated unless the return contract is specifically a byte. Do not assume all boolean APIs use an arbitrary nonzero value.
entries.notes:
Scope: x86-64.

Related: CMP; Conditional jumps; cmovz.
Official references: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html

entries.title: Unsigned DIV and the high half
entries.definition: DIV r/m64 divides unsigned RDX:RAX by its explicit operand, returning quotient in RAX and remainder in RDX. For an ordinary unsigned 64-bit numerator clear EDX first. For a true 128-bit numerator the high half is meaningful; quotient overflow faults. DIV and IDIV use different interpretations and preparation.
entries.mental_model: The high half is part of the dividend, not optional scratch space.
entries.return_value: DIV leaves arithmetic flags undefined; RAX/RDX are implicit inputs and outputs.
entries.gotchas: Check divisor zero before division. Clearing EDX is wrong when you meant a negative signed numerator or intended a nonzero high half.
entries.notes:
Scope: x86-64.

Related: idiv; IMUL.

entries.title: System V stack frames and call alignment
entries.definition: A stack frame holds saved registers and local storage for one call. On ordinary System V AMD64 entry, RSP is 8 modulo 16. Saving RBP with PUSH makes it 16-aligned; a further allocation divisible by 16 preserves alignment before nested calls. Undo the allocation and saved registers in reverse order. Frame pointers are optional, but useful when learning to inspect stack slots.
entries.mental_model: Track an exact byte ledger: return address, saves, locals, outgoing arguments. Alignment follows the ledger.
entries.return_value: PUSH/MOV/POP/RET preserve arithmetic flags; SUB/ADD update them.
entries.gotchas: Never overwrite [RBP+8], the return address in this frame. Windows shadow space is separate. Red-zone values cannot be kept across calls that may use that area.
entries.notes:
Scope: linux-x64.
Debugger: break demo, print $rsp%16 at entry and after PUSH, then x/4gx $rsp. This ELF learning function omits DWARF unwind annotations; frame inspection is not a production unwinding guarantee.
Related: CALL and RET; Windows stack and unwind contracts.
Official references: https://gitlab.com/x86-psABIs/x86-64-ABI
https://www.nasm.us/doc/nasm13.html

entries.title: RIP-relative addresses and indexed globals
entries.definition: DEFAULT REL changes NASM’s default for eligible registerless memory references in 64-bit mode. Explicit REL makes intent visible. It does not turn every immediate address, external reference, or indexed operand into position-independent code. RIP-relative encoding has a signed 32-bit displacement and no scaled index field. Obtain a local relative base with LEA, then index from that register.
entries.mental_model: First locate the object relative to code; then walk within the object using normal base/index addressing.
entries.gotchas: mov rax,label loads an absolute address and can require a relocation. GOT/PLT rules and symbol interposition matter for external symbols; DEFAULT REL is not universal PIC.
entries.notes:
Scope: x86-64.

Related: LEA; Memory addressing; Object files and linking.
Official references: https://www.nasm.us/doc/nasm13.html

entries.title: BITS, object format, and CPU mode
entries.definition: BITS 16/32/64 controls how NASM encodes instructions; it does not switch the running CPU mode. The executable loader and privileged system setup establish the actual execution environment. The object format -f elf64, elf32 or win64 determines relocation/container conventions. A flat binary is raw bytes and is not automatically a Linux or Windows executable.
entries.mental_model: Assembler encoding, file container, processor mode and OS ABI are four distinct layers.
entries.return_value: BITS and section directives have no CPU flag effects.
entries.gotchas: Changing BITS to 32 does not make a 64-bit process execute a 32-bit function correctly. Do not mix relocation formats at link time.
entries.notes:
Scope: x86-64.
Build: nasm -f elf64 demo.asm -o demo.o. Inspect: objdump -f demo.o and objdump -d -Mintel demo.o. Do not execute an object file directly.
Related: x86-32 integer functions; Windows x64 integer ABI.
Official references: https://www.nasm.us/doc/nasm08.html

entries.title: NASM constants, repetition, and macro expansion
entries.definition: The preprocessor transforms source before instruction assembly. %define substitutes tokens; EQU defines an assembly-time symbol value; TIMES repeats a data/instruction declaration. A macro can reduce repeated source but does not create a runtime function call or save registers automatically. Inspect a listing or preprocessed output to see exactly what expanded.
entries.mental_model: Distinguish writing source compactly from reducing the executed instruction count.
entries.return_value: Preprocessing has no runtime flags. IMUL here sets CF=OF=0 and leaves other arithmetic flags undefined.
entries.gotchas: A textual macro can change parsing in surprising ways. For teaching, keep macro bodies short and document clobbered registers.
entries.notes:
Scope: x86-64.
Preprocess with nasm -E demo.asm; list bytes with nasm -f elf64 -l demo.lst demo.asm. The example defines SCALE before use.
Related: EQU; Object files and linking.
Official references: https://www.nasm.us/doc/nasm03.html

entries.title: Object files, linking, and disassembly
entries.definition: Assembly produces relocatable object code; linking resolves symbols and builds an executable/shared object. A linker can report an undefined symbol even when assembly succeeded. An object disassembly shows instructions and relocations; a final executable disassembly shows resolved layout. Debug info connects machine addresses back to source but does not change the ABI.
entries.mental_model: Verify each boundary: source -> object -> linked program -> observed result.
entries.return_value: MOV/RET preserve flags. Tool commands operate on files, not CPU instruction state.
entries.gotchas: Do not interpret an unresolved object relocation as the final runtime address. ELF32, ELF64 and Windows COFF are not interchangeable.
entries.notes:
Scope: x86-64.
Recipe: nasm -f elf64 -g -F dwarf demo.asm -o demo.o; nm demo.o; objdump -dr -Mintel demo.o. With harness.c: gcc -g harness.c demo.o -o demo-test. Debug with gdb ./demo-test, break demo, run, disassemble /r demo, stepi, info registers. Read-only debugger exercises use your own process.
Related: GLOBAL and EXTERN; C harness and debugger.
Official references: https://www.nasm.us/doc/nasm02.html
https://sourceware.org/gdb/current/onlinedocs/gdb.html/Machine-Code.html

entries.title: C harness and a cross-ABI add2 lab
entries.definition: A C declaration is the caller’s contract with an assembly function. This System V leaf takes two long integers in RDI/RSI, returns their sum in RAX, and touches no callee-saved registers. A Windows counterpart needs RCX/RDX instead. Integer widths also differ across C data models: Linux x86-64 long is 64-bit; Windows long is 32-bit, so use explicit int64_t when comparing ABIs.
entries.mental_model: An ABI lets independently compiled modules agree about the same call.
entries.return_value: ADD sets arithmetic flags; function return contract is RAX.
entries.gotchas: A mismatched prototype can appear to work on small values and fail on larger widths. Signed overflow policy must be chosen by the caller/application.
entries.notes:
Scope: linux-x64.
Harness: #include <stdint.h> and <stdio.h>; declare extern int64_t demo(int64_t,int64_t); in main print (long long)demo(20,22) using %lld. Build object with nasm -f elf64; link using gcc. The verification harness in the task artifacts tests both positive and negative inputs.
Related: System V AMD64 calling convention; Windows x64 integer ABI.
Official references: https://gitlab.com/x86-psABIs/x86-64-ABI
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/x64-calling-convention?view=msvc-170

entries.title: Bounded array sum with an empty-input path
entries.definition: This System V function accepts a pointer to signed 64-bit elements in RDI and an unsigned count in RSI. It checks for zero before reading, advances by eight bytes per element, and returns a wrapping 64-bit sum in RAX. The caller must supply a readable array with at least count elements. An empty input performs no dereference, so a null pointer is acceptable only for that zero-count case.
entries.mental_model: Separate loop invariant from termination: pointer names the next unread element, count is remaining elements, accumulator is sum so far.
entries.return_value: ADD changes arithmetic flags; DEC supplies ZF for JNZ while preserving CF. Return flags are unspecified by the function contract.
entries.gotchas: This is not a memory-safety boundary against dishonest lengths. The sum wraps on overflow; detecting signed overflow requires an explicit policy.
entries.notes:
Scope: linux-x64.
Debugger exercise: watch RDI advance by 8 and RSI decrease. Run the zero-length case first. The validation harness also tests a single negative element.
Related: Memory addressing; Labels; ADD and SUB.
Official references: https://gitlab.com/x86-psABIs/x86-64-ABI
https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html

entries.title: Bounded byte-string scan
entries.definition: This System V function returns the index of the first zero byte, or the supplied maximum if none appears. RDI points to readable bytes and RSI is the maximum readable count. Unlike an unbounded strlen, every memory read is preceded by a bound check. It measures bytes, not Unicode characters; a multibyte UTF-8 character can occupy several bytes.
entries.mental_model: Check permission to read before asking what the byte contains.
entries.return_value: CMP defines comparison flags; INC supplies its own arithmetic flags but the next iteration replaces them.
entries.gotchas: The caller must still provide max readable bytes. A return equal to max means no terminator was found within the bound.
entries.notes:
Scope: linux-x64.
Debugger exercise: use x/4bx $rdi on valid input; observe the bound branch before the byte load. Tests cover empty, terminated and unterminated ranges.
Related: CMP; Conditional jumps; Memory addressing.
Official references: https://gitlab.com/x86-psABIs/x86-64-ABI
https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html

entries.title: Linux ELF64 hello and process exit
entries.definition: _start is a process entry symbol, not a C function called with a return address. This self-contained Linux x86-64 executable writes a fixed byte string to stdout and exits using raw syscalls. It treats a short write as failure for this small demonstration; a reusable streaming writer would loop. Syscall numbers, registers and error policy are explicitly Linux-specific.
entries.mental_model: The process is created by the loader and terminated through the OS; RET is not its exit mechanism.
entries.return_value: SYSCALL clobbers RCX/R11. CMP/SETNE construct the exit status. No function return occurs.
entries.gotchas: The exit syscall shown ends this thread; for multithreaded process shutdown see the Linux exit_group contract. This single-thread lab is sufficient here.
entries.notes:
Scope: linux-x64.
Build/run in a scratch directory: nasm -f elf64 -g -F dwarf hello.asm -o hello.o; ld hello.o -o hello; ./hello. Debug: gdb ./hello, break _start, run, stepi. No libc or network is involved.
Related: write syscall; syscall instruction; Object files and linking.
Official references: https://www.kernel.org/doc/man-pages/online/pages/man2/syscall.2.html
https://www.kernel.org/doc/man-pages/online/pages/man2/write.2.html
https://www.nasm.us/doc/nasm02.html

entries.title: Windows x64 integer ABI and leaf add2
entries.definition: Windows x64 passes its first four integer/pointer arguments in RCX,RDX,R8,R9 and returns a scalar integer in RAX. Callers reserve 32 bytes of shadow space for register arguments. A simple leaf function that neither allocates stack space nor calls another function can return without a frame. Nonvolatile registers include RBX,RBP,RDI,RSI,R12–R15; XMM6–XMM15 also have preservation requirements.
entries.mental_model: The same x86 instructions can obey different calling contracts; an ISA is not an ABI.
entries.return_value: LEA/RET preserve arithmetic flags; caller-saved RAX changes.
entries.gotchas: Do not pass Linux RDI/RSI arguments to this function. There is no Windows red zone. Windows C long is 32-bit; use int64_t for the 64-bit contract.
entries.notes:
Scope: windows-x64.
Cross-assemble: nasm -f win64 demo.asm -o demo.obj. Linking/running requires a Windows-compatible toolchain and caller; Linux validation checks object format and disassembly only.
Related: C harness and a cross-ABI add2 lab; Windows stack and unwind contracts.
Official references: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/x64-calling-convention?view=msvc-170
entries.summary: Windows x64 passes its first four integer/pointer arguments in RCX,RDX,R8,R9 and returns a scalar integer in RAX.

entries.title: Windows stack and unwind contracts
entries.definition: At normal Windows x64 function entry RSP is 8 modulo 16. A caller must provide at least 32 bytes of shadow space before making another call and satisfy 16-byte alignment in the body. With no earlier pushes/locals, subtracting 40 combines 32 shadow bytes and 8 alignment bytes; after a saved-register push the calculation differs. Nonleaf/frame functions require appropriate unwind metadata and constrained prologues/epilogues for production exception handling.
entries.mental_model: Compute stack space from your actual frame; 40 is an example result, not a universal constant.
entries.return_value: MOV/RET preserve arithmetic flags. A frame’s SUB/ADD would change them.
entries.gotchas: Do not ship a hand-written nonleaf routine without correct .pdata/.xdata or toolchain-supported unwind declarations. Shadow space belongs to the callee during a call; do not keep caller locals there across it.
entries.notes:
Scope: windows-x64.
Exercise on paper: entry RSP%16=8. No push -> reserve 40 before call. One 8-byte push -> reserve 32 before call. Add locals and extra stack arguments before recomputing. This page intentionally uses a valid leaf object rather than an incomplete nonleaf unwind implementation.
Related: Windows x64 integer ABI; CALL and RET.
Official references: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/x64-calling-convention?view=msvc-170
entries.summary: At normal Windows x64 function entry RSP is 8 modulo 16.

entries.title: x86-32 registers and Linux i386 cdecl
entries.definition: IA-32 has 32-bit EAX–EDI general registers rather than the x86-64 R8–R15 set. In the ordinary Linux i386 C integer calling convention, arguments are stack-based and the caller removes them. At entry [ESP] is the return address, [ESP+4] the first 32-bit argument, [ESP+8] the second. Preserve EBX,ESI,EDI,EBP and restore ESP. Modern platform stack alignment still matters, especially before nested calls.
entries.mental_model: A 32-bit function is a different binary/ABI target, not a smaller spelling of a 64-bit function.
entries.return_value: ADD defines arithmetic flags; EAX is the integer result.
entries.gotchas: Do not link this object into an ELF64 executable. BITS 32 does not switch a 64-bit process into compatibility mode. Windows 32-bit cdecl/stdcall conventions and symbol decoration need their own contracts.
entries.notes:
Scope: x86-32.
Assemble: nasm -f elf32 demo.asm -o demo.o. Inspect: objdump -dr -Mintel demo.o. A 32-bit C harness needs a compatible runtime; none is installed or assumed by this task.
Related: BITS, object format, and CPU mode.
Official references: https://www.nasm.us/doc/nasm02.html
https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/intel-sdm.html
entries.summary: IA-32 has 32-bit EAX–EDI general registers rather than the x86-64 R8–R15 set.

entries.title: Linux i386 process entry and int 0x80
entries.definition: Linux i386 raw syscalls use EAX for the service number and EBX,ECX,EDX,ESI,EDI,EBP for up to six arguments. The historical int 0x80 entry is distinct from the x86-64 SYSCALL ABI. This small ELF32 program exits with status 7; it makes no memory or device requests. Its _start has no function caller and must not RET.
entries.mental_model: Match syscall table, register width and executable target together.
entries.return_value: No normal return. Do not depend on flags across an OS service.
entries.gotchas: Do not copy x86-64 exit number 60 into an i386 program. Kernel compatibility support is an environment property, not an assembler option.
entries.notes:
Scope: x86-32.
Object check: nasm -f elf32 exit.asm -o exit.o; objdump -f exit.o. Possible link recipe on a suitable host: ld -m elf_i386 exit.o -o exit32. Execution was not used as validation here.
Related: Linux ELF64 hello and process exit.
Official references: https://www.kernel.org/doc/man-pages/online/pages/man2/syscall.2.html
https://www.nasm.us/doc/nasm02.html

entries.title: NASM versus GNU assembler syntax
entries.definition: NASM uses Intel-style destination-first operands and brackets around memory. GNU as on x86 commonly uses AT&T syntax with source-first operands, % register prefixes, $ immediates and size suffixes; it also supports an Intel syntax mode. GNU syntax for ARM/RISC-V is architecture-specific and is not NASM. The assembler and object target must both match the example.
entries.mental_model: Same operation, different source grammar; a mnemonic alone does not identify a dialect.
entries.gotchas: Do not blindly reverse every operand in ARM or RISC-V code. NASM does not assemble ARM, AArch64 or RISC-V sources.
entries.notes:
Scope: linux-x64.
GNU build: as --64 demo.s -o demo.o. Disassemble with objdump -d -Mintel to see the same bytes in another display syntax. Highlighting is GNU assembler here, not NASM.
Related: BITS, object format, and CPU mode.
Official references: https://www.nasm.us/doc/nasm02.html
GNU x86 syntax: https://sourceware.org/binutils/docs/as/i386_002dVariations.html

entries.title: Cortex-M4: Thumb registers and instruction width
entries.definition: Cortex-M4 implements Armv7E-M and executes Thumb instructions, including 16-bit and 32-bit encodings. Its ordinary integer registers R0–R12 are 32-bit; R13 is SP, R14 LR, R15 PC. Low registers R0–R7 have more compact encoding options. This is not the AArch64 X/W register model. STM32F401 contains a Cortex-M4 core, but the MCU memory map and peripherals are a separate reference.
entries.mental_model: Register width and instruction encoding width are different: a 16-bit Thumb instruction can operate on a 32-bit integer.
entries.return_value: ADDS updates N,Z,C,V. MOVS immediate updates N/Z with carry behavior tied to immediate encoding; the trace relies on ADDS final flags, not inherited C/V.
entries.gotchas: Do not paste AArch64 instructions into Cortex-M source. .thumb selects encoding; it does not initialize a vector table, stack, clock, or device.
entries.notes:
Scope: cortex-m4.
Assemble: llvm-mc -triple=thumbv7em-none-eabi -mcpu=cortex-m4 -filetype=obj demo.s -o demo.o. Disassemble: llvm-objdump -d demo.o.
Validation scope: cross-assembly/disassembly only. Expected execution state is a reasoned trace, not a hardware/emulator observation. No peripheral access or firmware flashing.
Related: Cortex-M4: calls, stack and startup boundaries.
Official references: https://developer.arm.com/documentation/dui0553/latest/
https://sourceware.org/binutils/docs/as/ARM-Directives.html
entries.summary: Cortex-M4 implements Armv7E-M and executes Thumb instructions, including 16-bit and 32-bit encodings.

entries.title: Cortex-M4: byte/word loads and explicit addresses
entries.definition: LDR/STR transfer 32-bit words; LDRB zero-extends an 8-bit byte and LDRSB sign-extends it. Memory operands use a base register with an allowed offset. Some encodings permit writeback, which changes the base as well as accessing memory. This function reads the first byte at R0, then the aligned word four bytes later; the caller supplies eight readable bytes of ordinary memory.
entries.mental_model: Keep the address, transfer width, extension rule and base-update rule separate.
entries.return_value: LDRB/LDR and this non-S ADD.W preserve APSR arithmetic flags. R1/R2 are scratch results; R0 becomes the sum.
entries.gotchas: Device-memory access has ordering and side effects not modeled here. Alignment support varies by instruction and system settings; use aligned word data and never infer an MCU peripheral address.
entries.notes:
Scope: cortex-m4.

Validation scope: cross-assembly/disassembly only. Expected execution state is a reasoned trace, not a hardware/emulator observation. No peripheral access or firmware flashing.
Related: Memory addressing; Cortex-M4: Thumb registers and instruction width.
Official references: https://developer.arm.com/documentation/dui0553/latest/
https://sourceware.org/binutils/docs/as/ARM-Directives.html
entries.summary: LDR/STR transfer 32-bit words; LDRB zero-extends an 8-bit byte and LDRSB sign-extends it.

entries.title: Cortex-M4: comparisons, branches and APSR
entries.definition: CMP sets N,Z,C,V as a subtraction without storing its result. On Arm subtraction C=1 means no unsigned borrow, opposite the x86 subtraction-borrow interpretation. BLT uses N!=V for signed less-than; BLO/BCC uses C=0 for unsigned lower. BEQ tests Z. Branches do not write those flags. The example implements signed less-than for R0 and R1, returning a full 32-bit 0/1.
entries.mental_model: The condition mnemonic chooses signedness; the register bits themselves do not.
entries.return_value: CMP defines NZCV; the branch consumes it immediately. MOVS changes N/Z, so return flags are not the original comparison.
entries.gotchas: An intervening flag-setting instruction invalidates a pending comparison. A returned integer boolean is more robust than promising flags across a function call.
entries.notes:
Scope: cortex-m4.

Validation scope: cross-assembly/disassembly only. Expected execution state is a reasoned trace, not a hardware/emulator observation. No peripheral access or firmware flashing.
Related: CMP; Cortex-M4: calls, stack and startup boundaries.
Official references: https://developer.arm.com/documentation/dui0553/latest/
entries.summary: CMP sets N,Z,C,V as a subtraction without storing its result.

entries.title: Cortex-M4: calls, stack and startup boundaries
entries.definition: AAPCS32 passes ordinary integer arguments in R0–R3 and an integer result in R0. R4–R8,R10,R11 are callee-saved; R9 has a platform-specific role. BL writes LR, so a function making a nested call must preserve its own return path. At a public interface the stack is 8-byte aligned. On bare metal, startup/vector-table/linker-script work establishes a valid initial SP and initializes data/BSS; a callable function object is not a complete STM32 firmware image.
entries.mental_model: A function contract begins after startup has made execution possible.
entries.return_value: PUSH/POP, MOV as assembled here, non-S ADD.W and branches preserve arithmetic flags; no flag-return contract is made.
entries.gotchas: Pushing only LR would move an aligned stack by 4 before the nested call. Do not confuse ordinary function saves with Cortex-M exception stacking, EXC_RETURN or interrupt handlers.
entries.notes:
Scope: cortex-m4.
This example is an integer-only AAPCS32 function. Hardware floating-point calling conventions must match the rest of a program; no floating-point or interrupt configuration is attempted.
Validation scope: cross-assembly/disassembly only. Expected execution state is a reasoned trace, not a hardware/emulator observation. No peripheral access or firmware flashing.
Related: Cortex-M4: Thumb registers and instruction width.
Official references: https://github.com/ARM-software/abi-aa/blob/main/aapcs32/aapcs32.rst
https://sourceware.org/binutils/docs/as/ARM-Directives.html
